I am giving it 2 stars. I think they are going in the right direction and improving the technology which I very much enjoy. Compared to pricking my finger and waiting 25 seconds or anything else I have done. I have had little problem getting my readings, the sensor works. Over time I have had problems with a sensor not working or even dead on arrival, but calling the Libre hot line always results in a new sensor being sent to me. I do not like this app however, it is probably a good start but if user control doesn't improve, I plan to move on. Background: I have type 1 diabetes, been diabetic for 34 years. Consider myself fairly stable. Never used a pump, so all injections. Been using the Libre 1 sensor since it first came out. Been on the 14 day Libre 2 sensor for about 3 months. Once this app became available, I was excited to start using it and it has now been about a month. Education: Electrical Engineer so very technically savvy. What I think needs to be improved: 1. Remove the limitation of user controls for sound, vibration, range limits, etc. In fact, add more options based on what different diabetic needs might be. This app was built for someone that wants to helicopter their child or a parent. and not let them be able to turn it off. If you are dealing with someone that needs help or can easily get themselves into a predicament, it makes sense that you want to set certain settings. This app assumes you can't make your own decisions. and needs everyone in your home, building, city to know if your blood sugar is high or low. 2. Make the alarms easier to dismiss. I use android and I lock my phone. So when the alarm starts going off I have to get to my phone, then I have to unlock it, find the alert icon at the top of the screen and then slide it it over to dismiss it. It takes a while. If I am in a meeting or somewhere I don't want to be a distraction, the last thing I want is a app that starts ringing to disrupt everything. If I could reach in my pocket and push one of the side buttons and have it stop, that would be acceptable. I do have a smart watch and the notification does show up on my watch with a "dismiss" button, but that is sometimes not easy to hit. 3. Along the same lines of making it easier to dismiss, make the dismiss button easy to get to (foreground) and then don't keep turning the alarm on every minute. Once I dismiss the alarm, I know about it, so don't remind me every minute and make me dismiss it again! Once my blood sugar was going low because I took too much insulin. I realized my mistake and found something to eat. About the same time my alarm started going off, I dismissed it. The alarm went off five more times in the time it took for the food I had eaten to raise my blood sugar. This is really annoying in the middle of the night!!!! Going back to the easy dismiss button, I have alarm apps that when they go off, they take over the screen (locked or not) and allow you to snooze or dismiss. This app should be able to do the same, make it easy to dismiss and then don't keep alerting me of something I know unless it is an option in the settings. 4. Allow the alarms to be vibration as an option. Right now the only option is to let the phone vibrate while doing a reading. See my notes above... I am one that prefers to knowing without announcing it to everyone around me. 5. Allow users to turn on/off the ultra low alarm or at least be able to set the range. Right now this is set at 55 mg/dl and you can not turn it off. I think it is a good feature to have but I also think that every diabetic is different I personally don't black out (ever), I would rather set my alarm to 50 mg/dl. I am not saying take it out, I am saying give the user options. 6. Provide parental options. I do think there are times when a user might be a child or an older person that might not have the ability to control their diabetes themselves. In these cases, a caregiver or parent might need to setup options without letting the individual change them.

Would you like to play the card game War? You only start with Aces and Twos, but you can unlock a higher card every month! We promise it's a strategy game! I've been playing this game for 180 days. I have done reasonably well, placing in the Global top 5% of events, and top 25 of free for all events. Here are the pros and cons: 1. Logistics - There's a fun aspect of resource management/gathering in the game. You gather and buy buildings, research, and upgrades. Yay! 2. Events - Once you learn how to manage your sanctuary, you can start timing gains with events, allowing you to get more points, gains, and advancements. This is an addicting part of the game, and one I enjoy figuring out how to do the best at. 3. Puzzles - There is a story campaign that starts, but has no closure. When you reach the end, there is no story, cinematic, or other ending to the 24 levels you fought through. The story drops, and starts over at a harder version of level 1. What's more, the puzzles seem like a challenge until you realize your NPC enemies are either grossly over your power level, or easy enough to be able to be taken by the autoplay function. Sure, you can eek out a manual victory against a hard level once in awhile, but most of the time it is a matter of how much you have upgraded your heroes. 3. Theme - All over the place! Zombie game? Mutant spiders/scorpions? Godzilla mods... puppies and kittens to rescue?! What the hell is going on?! They could do a lot by leaning into the zombie theme and making it immersive, instead of having bits of 10 different genres. 4. Combat - Back to my 'war' analogy. If you are fighting someone who has more stats than you, you lose. There is no strategy, just a greater than/less than result. They do have a Rock, Paper, Scissors mechanic where Riders/Fighters/Shooters have a weakness against one and an advantage over another, however after a certain point that benefit becomes negligible. If you are fighting someone a sanctuary level or two higher than you (I am level 51, Sanctuary level 27), be prepared to lose 100-200 troops for every 1 you take down. When you lose a fight badly, they pop up an advertisement to 'avenge yourself', selling you a bunch of resources and healing speed ups. However, there is absolutely no way you will beat that target. There is no strategic lever to pull, you are just going to lose again. This means in the Alliance vs. Alliance events, or free for all events, there is not a strategy to implement to get ahead, you just have to stay in your lane, picking off the weaker sancs while trying to stay out of the crosshairs of larger ones. 5. Inconsistency - There are some weird bugs in the rally system. You can team up with up to 5 members of your alliance to take down Zombie Lairs. This seems like a cool team building event. However, there is a break in the game the devs refuse to acknowledge (despite screen shots being sent). The way you beat these is to have one person take the primary spot and send a strong troop. Others each provide 1 troop to take part and get rewards, but not have an impact. If you have the 2-6 spots send full troops, you'd think you'd take less casualties and do more damage. However, your casualties will go from 2-3K to 80K+, and damage dealt will be somewhat larger, but not worth the extra loss. This is one of many weird bugs. 6. Pay to Win - I have gotten reasonably far in this game without spending a dime. I like to play on skill, not my wallet, and am okay with others who can buy an edge/time with a few extra bucks. However, there are powerful heroes and equipment that cannot be earned in game. You have to buy them. Then once you buy them, you have to buy upgrades for them. When you get into the PvP arena (Hero Battles), there is no filter/search to challenge people at your power level. You are presented with other players who are 10-50% stronger than you, and get a small reward for losing. To compete, you have to pay. 7. "Customer Service" - An absolute joke. They brush off questions/concerns, and even wave off screenshot evidence.

This app is terrible. The support and instructions for this is just as bad. I tried for two full days to transfer my messages. This is the only way to do it. Apple Support sent me to a local shop, blaming my WiFi. The tech at the shop told me they have never been successful in this app working its way to completion. At that point, I had to decide if I wanted to switch to iOS and lose my message history or stay on Android. It doesn't make sense about the WiFi comment from Apple because the iOS is the one broadcasting and is the backbone for transferring them. If you don't need to migrate your messages, there are other apps to transfer contacts, photos, and other items. Use those instead. So you might want to try to migrate your messages only and then use the other apps to transfer photos, etc. If you are making the switch, here are some tips: * Don't activate your iPhone until this completes. Otherwise, you'll get texts, phone calls, etc. even though you're iOS device hasn't been fully set-up. If you do view your call log or texts, you'll have to go through the setup and then do a device factory reset and start the Move to iOS process all over again. * It uses a private WiFi SSID from the iOS device to the Android device. For no more than 5 seconds, the Android device needs to connect to the SSID. If it doesn't, it just continues and tries to use your WiFi but it never goes anywhere and there is no indication from either app that nothing is happening. * If you don't see a pop-up on your Android device that you connected to the SSID "iOS xxxx", then you might want to take a 3rd device out and then look to see if the iOS device is broadcasting it or not. There were multiple times I didn't see it broadcast so I knew to start over again. * If you have to start over, it is best to restart both devices. * Make sure that you leave both devices alone until the transfer finishes. For example, on your Android device, the Move to iOS app should stay on-screen the whole time. If you use another app or get a phone call on your Android before the transfer finishes, your content won't transfer. So maybe take the SIM card out and silence all notifications on your Android device. * The instructions say, "should stay onscreen the whole time". Does this mean that if you turn off the screen, everything stops? What about burn-in? Even so I would advise to just leave it on because anecdotally, it seemed to go further (until it didn't). It is crazy that Apple engineers have to have the Android app in the foreground at all times with the screen on to make this work. This seems like a relic from pre-2000. * Even though this doesn't work the first time, there is no mention of what happens if you want to only transfer messages only. My guess is that you then have to use other apps to transfer Photos, Music, Device contacts, etc. What progress indicators they have either constantly spins or there is a line that never fills up. At times, it may tell you how much longer it will take to complete, but if you triple that time and return to your device, it is still stuck on the same message. Perhaps they should have a progress indicator of how many kilobytes out of how many gigabytes are moving across the connection. Yes, kilobytes because it feels like waiting for a file transfer over a 14k modem. Once you do get the file transfer, there are no warnings like "the app stopped working due to.... " Good luck - hope you have better luck than me. I understand that Apple touts the security of iMessage but I would think that they would try to make this one of their most robust applications, not their worst.

Recreates board game well. Issue: Asynchronous (longform/non-live) games are a bad experience: • In async games, players do not remain in the game after their actions are performed. This means they must re-enter and re-load the game for every single turn, including every single round of draft. Load times become obstructively longer as games progress, leading load times to completely eclipse time spent playing the game, making the game a bloated timesink and far less desirable to play. • In async games, if a player misses their push notification, there will never be a reminder, often leading to games unnecessarily stalling out until the unwitting player is ejected from time out. This is a resolution which is not fun for anyone. A recurring push notification every 10 hours (or user-set duration) reminding players that 'It's still your turn' would prevent async games from stalling out. Additionally, a 3 day turn timer rather than a 45 day game timer would prevent extensive stallouts and would be far more appropriate for a game in which the number of turns per player can vary dramatically, based on how many turns they take in a round before they pass and how many rounds the game lasts. • In async games, drafting in turn order especially drags out the process, as players either are not notified to look at their options until it is their turn in the turn order, or players who look at information early must unnecessarily re-enter and re-load (which is a timesink) the game when it is their turn in the turn order to officially submit their selection. Notifying and engaging turn timers for all players at the start of each round of draft selection and allowing them to make their draft selection in any order would be far more streamlined. Additionally, this would increase the likelihood of async players drafting live if players could see who is online as well as who has submitted their selection, getting an idea of whether staying for the next draft selection round (and thus skipping an additional problematic re-load of the game) is worthwhile. • In async games, the final round of draft before making purchases is completely unnecessary — each person must login, in turn order, and then they are done. There is no action for them to perform, there is no new information for them to perceive. In a live game, the round serves to display, in turn order, all players 'receiving' their final card from an adjacent player. They simply receive their final card and may not even yet look at their ultimate purchase options. This is a timesink in general, but it worsens further when coupled with the inoptimal load times in the game. This should be removed entirely. Show an animation of passing through the turn order to live players instead of doing a login check - or better, don't do the drafts in turn order at all and remove this step entirely for everyone. Issue: It prohibitively challenging to determine whether there are 1 or 2 steps to the temperature tracker rewards due to the placement of the number. This requires exiting the game to google search an image of the board just to find out. The number should be moved to the side of the line or below the line, anywhere less obstructive, and the rewards should state the temperature at which they occur with a long press. ——— Asmodee replied: Hello! New version drops from 2 to 1 star; saw no advantages and now: can’t see where flights come from; check-in with KLM and can’t track bags. Necessary but terrible app, Review from Oct 2020: I’ve now made 5 transatlantic trips with the App, having used United and it’s app the last 15 years. Although it’s generally helpful and better than nothing; it often isn’t and needs work: 1. Started about 48 hours prior to the flight you can’t see the seat maps anymore except by check in. Why? It’s not critical to travel, but why turn if off? United lets you see even after boarding. 2. Speaking of check-in, if you start your journey with an airline partner, which during the pandemic coming out many other countries is pretty much a given right now, the app is of limited value even if most of the trip is with Delta. You can’t check-in, see boarding passes etc.. On one trip, I had registered with Air France so I could check-in on their app, but then Air France assigned those miles to their program instead of Delta’s which does me no good; 2 months later, it’s still not sorted out. 3. During a trip, the app frequently shows notices and delays that are inaccurate and confusing. Take for example a recent trip from Munich to St. Louis via Amsterdam and Detroit. At one point it said the flight to Detroit was delayed and I would miss my connection; click and it showed we had departed at 10:08 (accurate, seven minutes EARLY) and also showed our scheduled departure as 4:15 (which is not related to any schedule or reality). It then showed an accurate arrival time in Detroit which left two hours to catch the connection (even a disabled wheelchair driver could get someone to that flight). The follow on flight was delayed, but the app never really got any of the information correct; afterwards, it showed the correct arrival time as delayed but showed a inaccurate scheduled arrival time that was later than both the scheduled and actual arrival times (in other words, if you did the math yourself off the app, we were 30 minutes early instead of 40 minutes). I’ve seen these type error on 3 of 5 trips. 4. A neat feature is looking at where the aircraft is coming from, allowing you to get a picture of how tight things will be. Unfortunately I’ve only seen this link show up as one checks in and then only for the one flight directly prior to mine. That’s adequate for transoceanic flights but for short haul flights doesn’t give an accurate picture. In comparison, United’s app will allow you to look back several flights with a far better clue on how things are really going. With United, I’d literally seen problems ahead of time and changed a route to avoid them … that’s not likely to ever happen with the current Delta app. 5. It is buggy, for example in Detroit all the sudden it wouldn’t log me on and then locked me out saying I had to call customer support. They said they’d call-back in 25 minutes, but took 40, by which time I reset the password from a browser which fixed it. I’ve had problems with it several times. The app has promise and is better than nothing. But if I were picking an airline based on the app alone, I’d walk away from Delta (they’re safe still by the way, the service remains good for the price).

UPDATE 07 Dec 2021: **Changed from 4 stars to 2 stars** After over 10 years of Pandora, I have decided to cancel my subscription. While I love the service, too many issues have become egregious and/or ignored for an extended period of time. Basic management features have been ignored despite community complaints going back several years. Music continues to become unavailable, only available in radio mode, or censored - all seemingly at random. * Inability to manage playlists is unacceptable. It's not possible on the app, web interface, or desktop application. However, the ability to add a playlist to another playlist is available, so you can easily add a massive list of songs to another massive list... and if you do so accidentally, there is no way to reverse it other than remove EACH INDIVIDUAL SONG. How does this make sense? It's like the UI devs had a few good ideas and then phoned in developing the rest of the feature set. There is a thread complaining about this from 2019 and no feature to manage playlists has been added to date. Also unable to reorders songs easily without dragging through the entire list which is very burdensome on large playlists. * Inconsistent behavior - Adding a song to 'thumbs up' adds it to the bottom of the playlist, while thumbing up a song gets it added to the beginning of the 'thumbs up' playlist. This means the songs I've recently 'liked' are in completely opposite sides of my playlist if my method of 'liking' them differed, and if I want to move one from the bottom to the top I have to drag and drop it THROUGH THE ENTIRE PLAYLIST (which is only even an option from the desktop application) which takes a few minutes to move each song because it doesn't work smoothly for large lists (once again, no way to manage lists easily). * songs randomly becoming unavailable, radio mode, or censored - I have a LARGE number of songs on my 'thumbs up' playlist that were the original version and somehow turned into the censored version. It's something I've been complaining about to Pandora for almost the entire last decade and something they still have not fixed. They give some answer about rights changing around, but I think they have enough money to lock content for their users. I really don't care about the reason, it f***s up my experience and I'm done dealing with it. To make matters worse, a lot of the songs I really like randomly become 'radio mode only' so they only play if I'm listening to a radio stream. Not sure why I'm paying extra if the songs I really like won't play when I'm listening to a playlist. In a few cases a song simply says 'unavailble' and I can't play it on Pandora at all. Again, I'm not going to continue paying for a premium subscription for this type of experience. Looks like it's time to switch to Spotify. I don't recommend the game unless you are a die hard Nier fan who just wants more lore. Gameplay is too grindy. PVP is a dumpsterfire due to the recent changes. (If you are looking for Automata, Replicant or Drakengard characters. You already missed the first 2 banner. Drakengard with Zero is ending soon) The story, while excellent , are few and far in between. They are also really short. The mini events story? EVEN SHORTER! They are only a step above a Sunday comic strip. If you want to see ALL the main stories you are actually expected to have a strong solid team to JUST to finish chapter 12 of normal mode. (currently only 12 chapters are out) The difficulty scaling spikes hard between chapters, not newcomer friendly unless you whale for the good units or grind on side content for enhancement materials. While super strong EX characters exist, it's just not feasible to get those with just free characters and they are typically time gated by time limited materials/ultra rare drops. The game DOES provide you with enough gems to get at least 2 full pity gacha, IF you clear all the main and side content. Which is nice, if you actually know what the good units are. The battle mechanic is... different. Your character auto attacks regardless of your input. Your only "choice" is to decide when you activate their weapon/character/companion skills. Frankly I think it's just an unwieldy mess with how it's implemented. Auto battle games can work, but... you are only allowed to auto grind 10 battles. The gameplay is VERY grindy as mentioned by others. One of the things to grind for, the memoirs, are a pain to farm and to enhance them it's also layers and layers of RNG. RNG to get the good drop, RNG to get the good primary stats, RNG to get the good sub stats, RNG to successfully enhance the memoir (bigger chance of failing the higher you go), RNG to enhance the RIGHT substats. That's 5 freaking layers of RNG! And you want the good memoir sets in order to do well in PVP! PVP is sort of necessary because it allows you to consistently obtain very rare materials to build the OP weapon/character that you want each season. But the PVP aspect in season 3 changed for the worse. It used to be that even mid range players can comfortably farm points, now they merged brackets so top 500 are player characters. Usually that's not a problem, the problem is it's RNG (chance of chain attack) on top of RNG (chance of getting countered) on top of RNG (we don't know who attacks next)... Even skill proc is more RNG now according to some player statements. This is on top of already restrictive play styles that favor only 2 kinds of builds: agility or skill cooldown. So your choice is basically whatever variations between those 2 if you want to do well. If you enjoy theorycrafting or wacky builds for PVP, you won't have much to work with here.

I've made the regrettable decision to deprioritize notifications from this app. I love the idea and intentions! There's just not enough diagnostic information included to make an informed decision. I understand the desire to protect people's privacy, but I believe this app has gone too far in that direction. The default settings seem to be to lower false negatives, whereas I want something that lowers false positives. I'll leave the app installed in case I ever get covid so that other people can be notified. I would be happy to reconsider once my concerns are addressed. (Also, I would much rather communicate these concerns directly to the developers, but the only mechanism I can find for feedback is this public review.) Why? First off, there's the fact that the app only tells you how many days ago you were exposed. I can't find out anywhere whether this counter starts at day 0 or day 1. So, that's 24 hours of ambiguity right there. Then, I don't know how much time is being added or removed from the actual time in order to maintain people's privacy. The end result is that I get a rather large time range where I might have been doing a lot of different activities with varying risk profiles. It's too restrictive for me to assume the riskiest activity was the cause of the notification. Second, I couldn't find any way for me to test what the app thinks is 6 feet with my particular phone. My understanding is that's going to be different with each phone. I've been getting notifications that people around me haven't been getting. That's led to unnecessary suspicion. My phone just might be more sensitive, but I have no way of knowing or showing that. The final straw came from my second notification. After the first notification, I played it really safe, isolating completely for 9 days after exposure except to go get tested. I tested negative. Then, a few days later, I got a second notification whose time window overlapped with my isolation period. That led me to think the most likely candidate for this new exposure was when I went to get tested. If so, then I could easily be caught in a loop. By directing me to testing facilities, this app puts me around people far more likely to have covid than what I typically face on a daily basis. Besides making it more likely that I get another notification from that testing itself, this app also seems to be increasing the chance that I get covid in the first place. This negative feedback loop seems at odds with the app's intentions. All things considered, I believe this app is not right for my particular lifestyle. I'm already strictly following standard safety procedures of social distancing, masking up, vaccination, avoiding risky situations, taking calculated risks when necessary, etc. The default advice and settings seem to be increasing my risk and thereby the risk to the people around me. Other people, with different lifestyles, may come to a different conclusion.

This would be a decent app, but just from trying it out a little bit, there's a major problem that I can see if you want to use the free workouts and activity tracker. There is no way to preview the workouts. If you use, for example, a YouTube workout video instead, you can click ahead to any point in the video and get a glimpse of everything the workout involves. With the Planet Fitness workouts, if you click on any workout to open it up, it will automatically start you on the workout. No skipping ahead to see what it has (although on the side it has a view that shows you what the next couple of exercises are, but you cannot preview the whole thing). The app assumes you are doing the workout while it's playing, so whenever you exit the workout, it adds it to your activity tracker, and I can find no way to delete that automatically-added workout from your activity tracker. So if you're trying to track your workouts and calories, looking at any workout videos will mess that all up. They don't seem to understand some people may want to see what a workout video contains before they choose a workout to do. They need to add an option to preview and skip through the workout like a regular video, and it should definitely ask after going through a workout if you want to add it to your activity tracker, not just add it automatically with no way to remove it. On another topic, I think it's wrong for Planet Fitness to require you to have the app. I always had a key tag that I used to check in with at the gym, but when mine broke and can't go on my keychain anymore, I was told they aren't doing key tags anymore because of the pandemic, and you can only check in with the app. That doesn't make sense. A key tag doesn't hurt anyone because, just like the app, the member just holds it up to be scanned to check in. The member does not hand the key tag to the employee to check them in. It's also really annoying when companies assume you want to take up space on your phone with their damn app. There are way too many apps out there for us as people to be able to add apps to our phone for everything; therefore, apps should be optional, not a requirement in order to use a service. It also seems a bit discriminatory because not everyone who belongs to a $10-a-month gym is going to even own a smartphone or own one that has enough space to keep adding apps. I thought I would check out the workouts to see if I might actually get some use out of the app since I was forced to get it, but nope, it's totally illogical how it works for reasons I stated earlier. Does not inspire me to use it.

I preface this review for those of you who already are good with goals and are looking for an app for to-do lists and reminders that are slick and swanky and something fun. I have in the past used "Habitica," which is gamification of to-do lists, but basically, I already was a high wizard with all the pets and things, so I wanted to use something new. If you are like that, here is my take. Please note that this is me, and my opinion is subjective. I wanted something I could use that would help me keep track of tasks. My friend, who isn't, said this app had the best to-do lists and reminders and was fun. So, I thought, what the heck, let's try! You get reminders, and they are colorful, animated, and poetic. You also get mantras, and chapters, and so much fluff. I'm not sure I needed the fluff or wanted that part, but hey, it's there. I mastered the first few things in a matter of days because I'm good at that. I do that already. Most of the app is for personal care, self-care, and health. Little of it is for ambitious things, or housework subroutines, etc. Additionally, you cannot build weekly sub-routines nor build monthly or quarterly routines. But a small thing such as putting in a reminder every month to six weeks that include changing your air filters, checking your water filters, and replacing the baking soda in the fridge, well that is impossible. The coaching was not something I needed or looked at, nor was any motivation stuff; I only came for lists. I also had no interaction with extras. What finally got me to uninstall and prompted this review was this scenario I had two days in a row where life had an emergency that overlapped the daily routine I usually did. Later in the day, both days, the routine was done, just not logged when it usually was set for. So the third day, I logged in, and I got 10 minutes lecture routine I could not get rid of. It told me that I was failing my goals and addressing "The elephant in the room." When I tried to get out of this subroutine, it'd show back up repeatedly overlapping my lists. This routine even had a different voice; this was a man telling me I was in the wrong, not the normal friendly lady voice it'd been using. I'm not 6, and I don't need a man voice I've never interacted with, only showing up to tell me I'm failing. I know when I'm being "mom-splained" or "man-splained," and I don't like it any more than anyone does. Especially when I wasn't failing, I just didn't hit buttons in the order of the time they wanted me to. I canceled it, and I'm not going to go back.

I agree with "Alexander Mittelstorb". I have paid for the advanced features, and it is running on an Android head unit in my car. Maybe that's when you get booked in Slovakia (and the USA?), but the rest of the world is different. Sygic is now completely useless for me and has turned my head unit into a very expensive radio. As well, all of the customisable warnings have disappeared to be replaced by discordant beeps. It used to say "Over the speed limit", but now goes "Beep! Beep!". How is that an improvement? The Graphics lacked colours and the 3D buildings after the update. It looked terrible. They returned after a manual map update. But the coastline is atrocious. The "ocean" is over 10km from the land, so bayside streets end in the middle of nowhere. It doesn't know when sunset is now. I'm sure that used to work. It now gets both Sunrise and Sunset late by about 15 minutes. So I'm blinded by the "daylight mode" for 15 minutes every night now. I'm at 145E (Melbourne, Australia), but it seems to be calculating for 140E. How can it get that wrong? It also crashes on start every now and then now (didn't used to). It also locks up on startup saying "Internet connection needed". The whole point is this is meant to run in a car without that. ... I've just heard back from Sygic. Apparently "This version is now using a completely new, modern programming core which will open more possibilities for the future." So it is a rewrite, and has left a lot out. Please fix all this ASAP or give me the old version. No, just give me the old working version. Update: October 2021. After 6 months, the latest version has restored adjustable speed limits and settable alert sounds. It still gets Subset wrong. Official Sunset here in Melbourne was 7:43pm. It finally switched to the Dark Mode at 8:13pm. That's 30 minutes late, and appropriate for Adelaide, which is 700km west. Background: My business has been using Teams as a daily driver for file collaboration, multimedia meetings, instant messenger and also as a phone system. We pretty much use every features of this application. We use the windows client and also the android client. We have been using since it's been out. Most people do not use Teams as a complete corporate phone system. Most of my issues are related to the phone system and using the android client. Issues about the android client: 1-Answering a call with a Teams Certified headset, the audio goes through the phone instead of the headset. It doesn't really matter if the device is UC or Teams certified. Tried two different android phones and about 5 different headsets. The apps does it with all of them. 2- Same issue if you get an incoming cell call while in a Teams meeting. Sounds and mic goes through the phone and completely ignores the BT device. Even if you decline the incoming cell call, you are still screwed. This may sound trivial, but imagine your attending a Teams meeting while driving your car. If you get an inbound cell call, the audio goes to the cell phone and you lose your ability to hear or speak in the meeting. Unless you want to stop on the side of the road to toggle your BT device back on with the small speaker icon at the bottom of the app. The android OS itself doesn't lose the BT connection, the app is simply acting up. 3-Delay(3-4 seconds) between answering a call and getting audio. 4- Latencies while in a call. Very annoying because you end up speaking on top of each other. 5- General bad call quality. I find myself rather surprised every time I get a good quality call. It happens once in a while. 6- You get a notification for an instant message and you can actually read part of that message in the notification zone but the actual message doesn't show up in the app. Sometimes have to wait 10-15 minutes before I can actually see it. 7- Ghost calls, you hear the incoming ring but can't pickup because the apps doesn't show the incoming call. 8- The apps doesn't really hang up when you press the hang up button at the end of a call. It does close the UI box but the sound channels remains opened and the other party can still hear until they hang up. The only way to really hang at the end of a call is to actually log out of the app or clear all resident apps from memory. Baseline, as a collaboration tool, it's good. As a phone system, you're better off with the windows client. Use the android client only if you absolutely must.

It's a pretty poor Pokémon clone. Very little distinguishes the various 'mon from each other. There are only 7 types, one of which is neutral to everything and the other have exactly two strengths and two weaknesses, all symmetrical (if you deal more damage to Mineral, you take less damage from Mineral). Nexomon have only one type each. Status moves are largely worthless, as most of them are the same and they only make your opponent miss one turn if they succeed. They're only good as rider effects on other attacks. Stat raising/lowering hardly does anything. The strength of a 'mon is determined entirely by its rarity. "Special" rarity (i.e. the starters) is the second-best, and you can catch them in the wild, so unless you're "lucky" enough to find a Legendary, you'll probably end the game with a full party of starters. There are different moves, but they hardly matter, with one exception (to cheese the final boss, which is a seriously terrible fight otherwise). There are only two types of "Nexotraps," and the one with 100% catch rate costs premium currency. The other one has a terrible catch rate, and the game never tells you how to improve it. I was weakening 'mon and using status moves on them, but I have no idea whether that actually helped. Catching Legendaries is awful; they just appear randomly in the wild, no story or anything, and they seem to have about a 2% catch rate. I found one and it took me about 50 traps to catch it. Speaking of missing information, the game tells you very little about the moves. They have varying damage and accuracy, but the game doesn't tell you what they are. Some inflict status effects, but you can't tell without actually trying them whether they also deal damage and what the status success rate is. And you better memorize what all your moves do, because you can't check in combat. You also can't check the moves of 'mon in storage, you have to put them in your party. Difficulty is very low. You get a lot of healing items and a lot of money, so you can always come back. Enemies always choose moves at random, even bosses, so you can beat them by using any strategy at all. The exception is the final boss, which also uses no strategy but one-shots you unless it hits you with an element you're strong against. It's not easy but also doesn't so much require strategic play as luck, patience, cheese, and a whole ton of Max Revives. On the plus side, the plot is okay. Nothing earth-shattering, but on par with most Pokémon games. Overall I find this game very hard to recommend.

About the only good thing to say about this app is that it's cheaper this year to watch NHL games this year than last year's NHL+ subscription. Otherwise this ESPN app should be renamed to "ERROR RETRIEVING CONTENT", because that's what comes up every time there's a commercial break during the hockey game. I have to quit and restart the stream, repeatedly, until the commercial break is over. When it actually works the ESPN app is slow, and manages to get pretty much everything wrong that could be gotten wrong, as far as its user interface. I specified which hockey team I follow. Is it too much to expect the app to feature tonight's game up and front, and make it easy to stream the team's telecast in one click? Of course not. That will be too much sense. But all this seems to do is put up some random bit of team-related news, tucked away in some corner. The home page still shows some random sports event, first, that nobody cares about. Ok, let's say I must make a bunch clicks to pull up a list of all currently live streams: and it's a few minutes before gametime. Maybe, just maybe, I could watch the end of the pre-game show? Nope. The stream becomes accessible at precisely on the o'clock and not a second earlier. If I click on the stream even a second earlier, I get scolded and reminded of the game's starting time. Ok, I have to sit and wait, and count off the seconds, and try again, right? Nope. I have to figure out how to refresh the page, so I can finally get the stream (unless it's in a commercial break), otherwise I still get the same "yo, fella, your game starts a minute ago" popup. And after all that, adding insult to injury: it's a random spin of the wheel whether I get my team's or the opposing team's stream by default. Drawing the short straw means a few more clicks to switch streams. Really, this is amateur hour. And when the stream starts it tends to glitch for a little while, before things settle down. Last year NHL+'s authorized Kodi app gave me perfect, glitch-free streams, 100% of the time, on the same Android TV device where this native ESPN app struggles to get in gear. It does, after a while, but it's still noticably slower and lagging compared to NHL+'s. Last year NHL+ had nearly every one of my team's games. This year there are noticable gaps. With ten games into the season ESPN+ did not carry two of them. Fail. But, it's cheap, so I guess I get what I'm paying for.

NOTE: Critique en français, followed by an English review at the end. Apologies for the length, Google Play doesn't seem to honor line breaks. *FRENCH*: j'ai passé un an et demi sur ce jeu, dont plus d'un an à désespérer en attendant l'ajout de nouveau contenu de campagne ou quoi que ce soit de différent de l'habitude... Mais Gamesture n'a travaillé que deux choses : les boss du weekend, et les nouveaux équipements qu'ils tentent de vous faire acheter par tous les moyens, sans qu'ils n'apportent grand-chose à la puissance du personnage. De toute façon, ce n'est pas bien compliqué : si vous voulez monter dans les leaderboards il faut d'abord choisir un serveur dépeuplé (Veterans ou Asia uniquement), puis passer plusieurs heures par jour à entretenir un compte principal ainsi qu'au moins un compte associé qui vous apportera des gemmes. Parce que sans gemmes, pas de répit dans le jeu. Quand bien même, il vous mangera des dizaines de milliers de gemmes, voire des centaines, si vous voulez être compétitif - sur un serveur déserté ! Pour ma part, j'ai atteint la première place après un an d'efforts, puis j'ai laissé tomber le jeu parce qu'il n'y avait rien d'autre à faire, et que les quelques changements occasionnels ne sont là que pour rendre le jeu encore plus invivable pour les joueurs F2P. Seule qualité rédemptrice, à mes yeux : la musique du jeu, qui est magnifique. Mais en gros c'est juste un morceau de deux minutes qui tourne en boucle, et qui ressemble beaucoup à une musique de Star Wars. Ah, et puis la communauté bien sûr... Les gens dans le jeu sont souvent adorables. Faites-leur plaisir, incitez-les à changer de jeu. Je ne sais pas si c'est le syndrome de Stockholm, ou la peur du coût irrécupérable (sunk cost fallacy), mais ils font parfois peine à voir. *ENGLISH*: this game sucks. Don't let yourself get sucked into it, or at least join a deserted server like Vets or Asia, maybe you won't have to sink too much money into it. Otherwise, be prepared to pay forever with absolutely zero payoff. If you really want to experience the game, enjoy the music and try to finish the campaign in easy mode, then maybe in hard mode if you're nostalgic about it. Then call it quits, because the endgame is a massive weekly running gag. If you're into constant disappointment, then by all means try it. Because yes, the team keeps promising tons of incoming content, and yet it never sees the light of day, because they basically have 40 'marketing directors' and just one developer, widely suspected to be a duck, doing more quacking than hacking.

Update: a month after my original review (3 star), I have to downgrade it to 2 stars. I still enjoy it, but I know that will change. The reward is always $300 + a bit more if you pay to play or have to watch an add. With some items costing north of $2000, you have to match a whole lot of tiles. There is no way to increase your $, except to a once a day ad for $485. So you play. A lot. And you watch ads. A lot. I've been playing this game non-stop for the last month. It feels VERY beta-ish. The nice part is it's a different sort of match three from what I usually, which I really welcome. Having this as a tile match where the tiles are stacked is much preferable to the Candy Crush sort of matching. The problems are when you get into playing regularly. The mechanics are good and the designs are mostly good. A month long subscription is on special for $4.99, and that's a good value. The regular rate is $9.99, and that's definitely NOT a good value. AFAI can tell that only buys you access to a few groups of "watch this ad and win a reward" and a few other things. Hardly something worth paying for. And definitely NOT worth the $9.99 price tag. The Wheel of Fortune is really limited in what you can win. Two of the rewards are for items I'm not sure what they are. for. You are given an option to re-spin if you watch an ad, and that's a welcome option. Ditto the Mystery Gifts you get after playing a match. I've amassed a hefty collection of neat items that I can't seem to use. The only time I was able to use any of them was in the first couple of design scenes. I'm now on my 7th scene, and there's nary a place in sight for these decorations. The good news is you are given a chance to add to daily to gems, lightbulbs, coins and free play time. They've also recently added a way to increase your stash of gems by watching ads. The beta feeling is because this game is rough around the edges. There are things like the decoration items that just don't have an explanation. Lack of options on the Wheel is a real oversight. Nothing to spend gems on makes it feel rather pointless to continue adding to your collection. This game has real possibilities, but the developers need to work on it. Hopefully they will (and will change the price point for membership!)

As so often with Google software, this shows promise, but doesn't quite deliver. A brief flirtation with Pikmin Bloom left me with Google Fit active, and I found myself benefiting from it's encouragement, but disappointed by the Artificial Intelligence version of "Heart Points," which in typical AI fashion, seemed to give artificial and unpredictable results. But I was encouraged enough to buy a fitness band, which I hoped would provide more and better encouragement. It did, sort of, so I returned it and bought a Mi Band 6, which has met all my expectations, needs, and wants. Being on my wrist, it doesn't quite count steps the same as the phone in my pocket, especially since the band doesn't start counting until you've been moving for a bit. So I was not surprised, that Google Fit counted more steps than the band. Until yesterday. Midday yesterday, after a nice walk, I was happy with my arrangement. But later on, I realized that Google Fit had completely lost the mid-day walk, showing activity before and after that, but with only a few steps of the mile-plus beach walk and hill climb (I was already disgruntled that it hadn't given me any heart points for the hill climb - because I wasn't walking BRISKLY enough, I presume, even if my heart rate was at the high end of my target range). Today, I tapped on the Google Fit widget as it displayed 552 steps, and it opened the app to display 405 steps, which is what the widget displayed as I exited. Later on, the widget displayed 95 steps. This is not how I expect a fitness app to work. I don't know if this was because Google Fit updated yesterday morning, and broke something in the process, or because I added the "Notify for Mi Band" app the evening, and linked it to Goggle Fit at some point. I don't care. I just want it to work. I want Google Fit to count steps, and add to them as I walk, not throw them away. I want Google Fit to have an option use GPS to allow the AI to more accurately estimate exertion level, and use the heart rate as well if linked to a fitness tracker. Is that unreasonable? \\ Update: took screenshots of two phones after walk this morning, and one said 52 heart points and 5970 steps, the other 45 and 5674. Now they both say 49 and 1888. My watch says 5637 steps.. I think it is ridiculous that to retain my owned achievements I have to go in and manually adjust the record.

Disappointing. I had no trouble installing, configuring, or pairing with my new Reflect meter. Until I started actually doing blood tests. They didn't show up in the app. Nada. And no clear evidence whether the app is actually communicating with the meter at that time (if I change range settings, the app asks me whether to use the meter setting or app setting, but doesn't say when it got the meter setting). So I entered the data manually. Then I realized that I can only set "before meal." I test twice a day: before breakfast ("fasting" - 80-120) and before dinner (ummm ... "behaving"? - 80-130). I don't want "good" tags if I'm out of range, I don't want "bad" tags if I'm in range. I did another test this morning, and instead of entering the reading manually, I started playing with the phone's bluetooth settings, which show the meter is not connected. I clicked "+" to tell the phone to connect to the meter - it didn't. I disconnected the phone from my fitness band - still didn't. I poked around some more. I looked at the meter. It showed the most recent test result, acquired via bluetooth from the meter. Sigh. So I don't know if I just haven't been waiting long enough, if I need to disconnect my fitness band, or if I need to randomly fool with bluetooth settings. But once I get that working, I still will have the most basic problem that the app won't accurately tell me whether or not I am in my target ranges half the time. So far it seems like all I've gained by upgrading from a OneTouch Ultra is smaller blood drops. Oh - and the meter setting time from the app beats the heck out of the Ultras, where I refused to adjust for daylight savings or correct for time drift because setting the time was such a hassle. (Anyone else remember connecting by serial cable and getting a message that the meter time and computer time didn't agree and you needed to manually reset the time? Sheesh louise - why couldn't they just ask if they should correct the meter to match the computer?) What it all the fancy and elegant super-features of meter and app don't amount to a hill of beans if the app and meter won't: consistently tell me if I am in range. If I need to disconnect the fitness band or fiddle with bluetooth settings every time I want to sync, I'll only be syncing once a week, if that. [Google Pixel 3a, Android 12]

As a free app, it gets the job done. I gave the prpo version a shot, as I wanted the ability to do custom alternate tunings, which was actually pretty cool. If it wasn't for this next little thing, I would rate 4 or 5 stars. Unfortunately, you can't just buy the app. Nope, you will pay 5 bucks a month forever, in order to have the ability to use the pro version. Thats insane. Greedy. I used the free version of this app for years to quickly tune a guitar in the off chance i had to. However, paying 5 bucks a month in perpetuity to have an app on my phone that I might use occasionally is a hard pass for me. I didn't notice it was a recurring fee until they were already into me for about 20 bucks. I thought the paid version was a one time purchase of 5 dollars, not a subscription! I would have bought the app outright, for probably more than 5 bucks. Heck, I'd probably spring for 10 dollars ONCE, but not to basically pay a rental fee to have the ability to access the app. I could have just gone and bought a pretty decent ACTUAL physical guitar tuner for what these people got me for with their recurring monthly fee. You guys, recurring fees are not really justified for this type of thing. If the content were dynamic and changing from day to day, like a video streaming service, sure bring on the fee, but an app that basically takes the place of a physical item I can literally purchase and hold in my hand is pretty sleazy and scammy, and is an obvious "Gotcha" attempt to sucker people into unknowingly paying at least one recurring monthly fee, or however many you can get away with before people realize its a subscription, and you can't just buy the app outright. Because of that, this potentially useful app gets dropped to the lowest possible rating, as well as incurring the deepest level of contempt I have for this business model and those who practice it. **TLDR: hard pass on recurring monthly fees to use a guitar tuner app. free version is ok. read the fine print and don't get suckered. ** Lastly, here's an idea- maybe don't try suckering people. Resist the urge to make a quick buck off of unsuspecting people. A good product ought to sell itself, not be used as a ploy to trick people into subscriptions so you can leech off of them. 1/10. Would definitely not use again.

I just signed up, so my review is based strictly on the set up process. I have heard good things from others, and I think this app/card/program will be helpful with my child. BUT the signup process is very "scammy." Not only the upsell of trying to get you to sign up for various higher cost plans that include investments (so many push notifications until disabled!) The bigger issue is the "standard" vs "customized" card. As you are setting up, every step directs you back to the customized card. There is NO WHERE to set up and order a standard card. What they don't tell you anywhere in the process of signing up is that you get a standard card automatically once your bank sync verifies. Indeed, I got a push notification after I was able to verify my bank that told me my "next step" was to order the card and it directed me to the customized card. I looked everywhere for how to get the regular card that doesn't cost extra. No info on the app, no confirmation email telling me it was automatically ordered. I texted the number provided on the app for help. To their credit, customer service was quick to get back to me and they let me know that the standard card was automatically ordered. They also went to my account to verify for me that it was indeed in process. Now WHY CAN'T I get that same info on my own account?! This is clearly designed to TRICK YOU into getting the customized card. The app directs you to do that multiple times during the set up. Nowhere does it tell you, that you already have a regular one coming. And you have to actually speak to customer service to verify a standard card was ordered since there was NO CONFIRMATION of this in my email nor in my app. I told customer service to please pass along my feedback as this comes across as, at best, an unclear and frustrating system, and at worst, VERY SHADY. Please change the process to be TRANSPARENT. You shouldn't have to dig so deep to find out that the customized extra fee card is actually....completely optional. I'm sure they make a lot of extra money of this setup but for me, it is a big turnoff. I will look for a system that is more transparent about additional optional fees.

Shooting an email to your subscriber base or raising a notification periodically through your application explaining what the current major issues are along with a meaningful explanation of what progress is being made and what the plan of attack is would be a much more appropriate response. ANDROID 12 BREAKS THIS APP. Unfortunately, the original developer has left and the people maintaining the app now do not appear interested in keeping it updated. I reported the below problem and the company has not responded to my steps to reproduce. If you depend on the app syncing deleted files with the server on exit, like I have for the past 8 years, this no longer works in Android 12 and they won't acknowledge it, let alone fix it. Steps to reproduce: 1. Have two devices ready – one with Android 12 and one with Android 11 or lower. 2. Both devices have a pop3 email account in Aquamail PRO configured to leave the messages on the server after downloading them. 3. Both devices have Aquamail PRO configured to automatically purge deleted on exit. 4. On a PC, have a browser up with the inbox for that pop3 account. Use the same pop3 for the tests on both devices. 5. Send two emails to the pop3 account and then download messages on both devices and the PC browser. The two messages will appear in all three places (see step 2 above if they don’t). 6. Delete one email on the Android 9/10/11 device and hit the back button until you have exited the app. You will see a flash of the Aquamail icon in the upper left of the device as it UPDATES THE SERVER. 7. Delete the other email on the Android 12 device and hit the back button until you have exited the app. You will NOT see a flash of the Aquamail icon in the upper left as it updates the server, BECAUSE THAT IS NOT WORKING IN ANDROID 12. 8. Now go back to the browser on the PC and refresh. The email deleted from Android 9/10/11 is gone. The email deleted from Android 12 is still there. 9. Yes, I just did this. WITHOUT manually clicking purge deleted. Automating this process on exit is the reason I've been using the app for the past 8 years. Android 12 broke the app and they do not appear interested in fixing it. They denied the problem existed when I first reported it. I provided these steps to reproduce on Nov 16 with two follow up emails in the past month and have gotten no response. Time to see how far the competition has come since 2013...

I am a long-time player (4+ years). When I first started it was enjoyable, but took a frustratingly long period of time to earn enough coins to get new characters to play with, let alone gems to purchase rare ones. However, you could play any of the special events to the end, even if you didn't have the "lucky" characters. It was just harder and took longer to complete. And at the end, you always earned a diamond box, which holds the rare characters. You never had to pay to play (although you could if you chose to), and you could watch ads to get additional power-ups, coins and gems. It is generally still a fun game if you play just to play and don't care about advancing or collecting new playable emoji characters. Things appeared to improve when Jam City took over management of the game - they increased the ways in which you could get new characters, which means more frequent leveling up and acquiring of new characters. However, very quickly, they have turned it into a Pay to Play model. There are still more ways to collect the "regular" emojis. However, in the past few months, they have run special events where the "lucky" emoji isn't available to win or purchase, you don't win a diamond box (or any playable emoji) at the end. And they have set up the newest special emoji only in a box that takes HOURS of play to get complete the level where you can win it, and even then, you only have a 1% chance of winning it unless you want to pay for it. Additionally, they have increased the requirements to complete without increasing the time (and often decreasing the playing time). Combined with making it extremely difficult to get the special lucky emojis, playing events has become a slog and for most of us, impossible to finish. Many people on social media are saying this is the "Disney" way. IMO, it is not. Disney admits to charging premium prices - for "exceptional experiences". This is NOT a Disney level exceptional experience. IMO, I think Disney needs to review its licensing agreement with Jam City, as the recent changes to this game have made it miserable for many long-term players such as myself. I will no longer spend money for in-game purchases, just on general principle.

At first i thought this was an okay game. The story is nice but your dialog options dont tend to matter. Par for the course really. If you are willing to do some reading you can also find bit of lore scattered about which is super great. But, after getting further into it, i found some frustrating features. 1. Lightning strikes are not random. While they are not terribly damaging they are skewed to strike near you. They are very frequent when it storms and can knock you off cliffs which can kill you. 2. Swimming is frustrating because the zoning doesnt match up to the terrane. There are too many places where it looks like you should be able to just stand but instead you swim. If you run out of stamina you drown and it resets you to where you were before you started. 3. Stun lock. Freeze locks you in place. you have to tap rapidly on the screen to break free. But you can be frozen again quickly. This is especially frustraing when it rains because you can not avoid the wet effect so when you get hit by cold you get locked. This can kill you vs enemies that would normally pose no threat. 4.The game does not pause in cut scenes. If something nearby could agro you or an environmental effect is ongoing you can die. 5. Somethings can be approached before you are allowed to interact with it. This means some puzzles can not even be started till you find the right quest but there is no indication of this. 6. Some quests require you to interact with something like an item in your inventory but it will not tell you this. 7. Co-op is not great. You cant get help with about half the quests. Really you can only do daily stuff with friends. You can also be locked out of co-op by starting certain quests. There is not indication which quests will do this and you can not quit the quest to reenable co-op. Likewise you can not interact with NPCs at all while in co-op mode. So no shopping or turning in quests to NPCs if needed. All in all it was an okay game but the frustrating features just keep popping up taking you away from the enjoyment.

When I ordered them a second time, I used my friend’s address because she lives in a building with an attendant. The next day, they were shipped overnight to my friend’s apartment from San Diego, CA. When I got the delivery notification, my friend went to check for the package. And perhaps a bit less unsurprisingly, the package was not there. When I again requested the proof of delivery from USPS, I realized her neighbor (from up the street) signed for the package. They are number 49, and she is number 205. Poshmark, of course, gave me the “we are sorry to hear you have not received your order…” response and will probably refund me. Beyond that, however, I can’t help but notice the parallels: both sellers shipped these boots out within 12 hours of purchase; they each shipped them overnight; Poshmark failed to authenticate the boots both times; both USPS postal workers let people sign for the packages at the wrong residence on the right street. Further, the sellers’ can’t profiles seem fake (there are no other listings, very few followers, and they used the same mock photos for these boots). On the other hand, these guys would have needed to hack USPS’s website to get the tracking history, the signature, and the proof of delivery functions to work correctly. So, there is that. Moral of the story? Either USPS is terrible, Poshmark has spam sellers, or both (it's probably both).

Making fans do your marketing for a small chance at a paltry reward is bad practice. We don't want to shill for a company that shows no appreciation to fans. miHoYo needs to put a team together specifically for listening to complaints and criticism. The players have been begging for many common-sense changes and other much needed improvements and feel ignored and unheard. It is a beautiful game with interesting story, but no end game content to speak of. Major update content tends to be done within the first week or two of release. Time-gating isn't the solution here. Need increased energy caps or energy regen rate improved. If you're going to play, I'd advise to keep it casual, or youll run out of things to do. As far as gacha games go this is the most punishing grind I've seen. Insanely low drop rate for decent artifacts, high cost for character wishing especially compared to rewards if not spending large amounts of cash. Be prepared to fight the same fights hundreds of times without getting what you are looking for. Forget about 5* character constellations and forget about getting the featured weapon for any 5* character you do get unless you are whaling or have the patience of a saint. The grind from adventure rank 55-60 takes something like 3 years of daily play without paying, and the rewards are a joke considering the time investment. Most major complaints would disappear if they improved energy regen from 8 minutes to 4-5 (and/or) tuned artifact stat drops 10-30% better, implemented a repeatable randomized enemy dungeon/raid system with high difficulty rewarding just 5-10 primogems per run, add more sidequest type content, and make co-op good for more than just a 5 minute domain run. Could add a lot of other common complaints, but don't really see the point as they are never addressed. For clarity, these aren't just "my" complaints, just a few of those I see repeated most frequently within the community. A significant portion of the player base have a love-hate relationship with this game. We love it, invest our time and money into it, and genuinely just want to see improvements for it to reach the potential it has to be so much better. Will update review accordingly if improvements are made.

Terrible update. -H2H is not fun anymore, too many easy chances and you will get penalized 99% of the time. Most games end in 10-15 goals from each side. They don't give you your chance percentages beforehand either. -Absolutely NO offline modes that you can consistently play, only 2 game modes are offline and both require you to wait 24h to refresh after you complete it (You can easily complete it in 10 minutes each). -Gameplay is very janky, slow, tedious, and all in all, not fun. Absolutely no pace difference between players like Adama Traoré and your basic slow defender. -No sense of accomplishment in offline H2H as scoring goals against the bot is relatively easy especially against the lower rated teams (I beat 84 rated Atlético Madrid 4-0 in 1 half with a 78 rated squad). -New recommended section in the Transfer Market zone would've been a great addition if it wasn't for the fact the section doesn't show you affordable players. -You can't search by price anymore in the Market either, very unnecessary to take that out and makes the whole process of the market much more annoying and time-consuming. -New exchange section is a great addition, as is the chants section and the commentary section, and I liked the fact that they made it optional to use it and which commentary language you want to use. -Friends don't stay added from previous years, and the max. of 32 friends is useless and needless, although this one has been here for the previous year. -Menu is very nice, quick and simple to use. -Training players is much more compact and simple, unlike last year where you had training overall, ranks and additionally skill boost upgrades. -Game is still wildly pay to win, but this was expected as it is an EA sports game. -New seasons update is neat and helpful to earn additional rewards. -The new substitutes feature is very good but surprising it wasn't there before. So is having the ability to change corner and free kick takers. -New Free Kick and penalties mechanic is stupidly hard, and the fact you don't have a tutorial to help you learn the new process is baffling. All in all, terrible update bar a few nice additions. 2/10 game.

This review is only taking into account the Medium mobile application - users leaving negative reviews because they are unhappy about a paywall shouldn't be leaving reviews here, since this is a company standard, not just app-related. ****************************************************************** I have only started using Medium as a writing outlet this month (Nov '21). I routinely write remotely, when away from my desktop, so I downloaded the app. It wasn't long before I saw the application lacked seemingly basic features, which prompted me to write to Medium customer service to inquire into those features that would be helpful, yet are missing. ****************************************************************** FIRSTLY, I tried to remove line breaks in between paragraphs, with a desire to turn two into one. I placed my cursor at the lead of the second paragraph, clicked backspace and, nothing. Removing a line break doesn't appear to be an option in the mobile app. ****************************************************************** NEXTLY, as I was attempting to remove the line breaks, I inadvertently added the 3 dots (add-a-section). I tried to remove them, but this doesn't appear to be an option in the mobile app. ****************************************************************** LASTLY, I tried selecting ALL text in my story draft, but that only selects one paragraph at a time, telling me once again, this doesn't appear to be an option in the mobile app. ****************************************************************** I received a response from support the next day, and they're response was "unfortunately, the app editor is more limited than the desktop editor and some of the things you are trying to achieve are not currently possible. I've shared your feedback with the responsible team so they can take it into account for future developments." ****************************************************************** I am certainly not a professional developer (I'm barely a novice), but this app launched for Android in 2015, which means for 6+ years these features have been missing - I can't imagine these are going to be integrated any time soon. ****************************************************************** Amongst the many hundreds of reviews YTD 2021, Medium has responded to a total of seven (7), which is not uncommon for app developers, but I like to see companies doing this more often than not because it tells me they care about their application and its improvement. ****************************************************************** For reference purposes: I am using Samsung Galaxy S10+, running Android 11

If you want a quick review I will say that this is a great smartphone game, with compelling mechanics and lots of fan-service for people who enjoy the 'TenSura' series. I had lots of fun casually playing it while doing other things. For the quick review, we can leave it at that. But for a long review I can't say that it's not held back by outrageous "micro" transactions, and a massive number of technical issues. I played since the day after launch, since for a full day when it released the game would error back to it's title screen whenever it tried to load. I've had a great time and managed to complete what is as of November the main story and get deep into many different events. However I had technical issue the entire way, crashing, graphics glitches, and simple menus would frequently break. This reached it's worse when after an update, the game for some reason force re-installed itself. Causing me to lose all my save data. I contacted customer support, spent 3 hours filling out an overly long forum, only to have to wait almost a month for them to tell me they couldn't do anything. (This is after a long time of trying to find a customer support I could actually contact personally, rather than dealing with those simple "Frequently Asked" areas.) Needless to say I'm not going back into the game. This is a simple issue that shouldn't happen in a modern smartphone game. One example of a game that has a simple fix to this would be "My Hero Academia: Strongest Hero", which while having it's own issues, at least connects to your Google account, so you can reinstall the game on any device and keep your save data. 'SLIME - ISEKAI Memories' needs a system like this and I really don't think it would be that hard to implement. To finalize all my points within a conclusion, this is a promising game held back by what is possibly a rushed development and poor decision making. I hope that this game can become something great as it updates further and fixes the basic issues, that have caused me to abandon the game.

Arknights always had very glaring issues but I decided to ignore them and stick with the game as I collected characters, utilized them to their strengths, and grew to like to them. The gameplay was barely interesting enough but very, VERY repetitive and with level caps gating every stage, with upgrading taking weeks upon months just to be able to beat the next few stages. Stamina is a thing in the game and you'll have to play old stages on the daily to gain the resources needed to level your characters and facilities. But instead of just using the stamina and getting the end mission rewards, the player must actually sit there and wait for the entire mission to replay itself and there's no way to speed it up past the x2 speed. And stages can take over 5 minutes to complete; weekly annihilations takes around 30 minutes of you just sitting around waiting for the stage to end, and you have to do this multiple times, meanwhile you can't use your phone for anything else. Such an utterly horrible and detrimental mechanic, that I assume was just implemented for the chance the stage fails, which can happen by the way, to incentivize the player to spend money to make their units stronger, or just plain sadism, which after playing some stages, there's definitely plenty of that. Now they've removed a voice actress, Ai Kayano, because of some controversy with China after she visited a Japanese shrine to commemorate WW2 veterans (yes just that). The audacity to remove her not from the Chine server only, but from the global server too and maybe even the Japanese server is ludicrous. This has been officially the nail the coffin for me that's been a long time coming. Ai Kayano voiced the character Platinum, which was one of my favorite and most used characters in the game and her voice lines were superb, as expected from Ai Kayano, but they've hastily changed it to a less known and less fitting voice actress which is hugely disappointing. If they're changing this now, imagine what else they won't mind doing in the future. I'm not staying for it and you shouldn't either.

This game is ok, it is fun, and runs well. It is a passive play kind of arena game, you set up your ships with tiles that do certain tasks and battle other ships to see who wins. Over all the mechanics seem to work well and the ship specifications work well to make them unique in play style. However, the game is slow and repetitive with almost no progression. Once you get to the Cruiser class ship (which is an appropriate amount of grind time) there is almost nothing to do. Between levels 18 through 24 there is little to do but wait and continuously battle. If your ship loses there is a long wait periods to play again, and if your rank is too high you sit in limbo either dying or winning every other match, which causes more waiting time. The designed timeline wasn't well thought here in the game. Blueprints and upgrade chips are hard to get which also prolongs progression. If you want to remove ads you buy a currency pack, I find that fair and have purchased 2 packs before, but honestly the value of your money into the game is not worth it. The game currency is not balanced for the value of money you spend at all. 3.99 will get you 100 currency, and something just like an extra hanger can cost 250 and over. That is almost $10 for nothing, something with no actual value. You are then hit with some sales ads that want you to buy a ship early for sometimes up to $20!!! Absolutely horrible and not considerate of players value. If you do ever buy one of these you'll probably have a great ship and quickly get to a rank where you skipped so much potential fun from progression that you will be stuck in limbo again I'm sure. To conclude, the game is fun, but there is a lot of lost potential from the listed above problems. In the end if you want 5 minutes to kill, open the app, playa couple rounds, come back 30 to an hour later while you go have fun on some other game.

I've been playing this game for over a year now, and I'm becoming increasingly disappointed. Since I first started playing, there have been numerous updates overhauling the UI and assets, and each time, they've gotten harder to navigate, lesser in quality, and - sorry to say - uglier. I wasn't going to write a bad review, because while they had made a couple of the menus wretched to look at, at least the home screen and a select few menus were still palatable. No more! No, now I'm met with an awful home screen, and every icon, for clothing and items alike, is terrible to look at. We went from having cute thumbnails for items to having poorly scaled-down versions of the 3D models that make it hard to find what you're looking for, and are much less visually appealing. As for the items, they're all washed out and have a fluorescent glare over all of them. Yuck. The UI is difficult to read, and now includes lots of annoying flashing that I'm sure is a nightmare for anyone with photo-sensitivity or epilepsy. The menus are very dark now, and when a sudden burst of white light happens every time you get a new item, the contrast against the background is blinding. They rearranged the layout of the menu, which has been the same for over a year. Moving Recollections to the opposite side of the room is downright criminal. For a game that takes up an obscene amount of space on my phone, I would expect it to at least look halfway decent. I can't bring myself to recommend this game to anyone unless they revert the menus and the clothing thumbnails back to what they were before. I may be inclined to delete the game and go play Shining Nikki instead, because at least that game maintains visual appeal. I could go on, but the biggest gripe I have right now is the visual changes with this latest update - I'll tear into the pricing of in-game items, the stories, etc. any day, but if they UI changes then this game would easily jump up a couple of stars.
