Editing this review to add some more feedback. I play this daily, it's a lot of fun and I'm so grateful they brought it to global. If I were to rate this game on pure potential it'd easily be a 5. The art is gorgeous, the gameplay is fun, the writing is entertaining, skip tickets are unlimited, and the devs are generous. That being said, it has its issues: 1. Equipment drop rates are awful - you'll spend hundreds of energy to only get a single drop of gear (mainly t3-t5). That's not right considering how many characters there are to gear, the hefty requirements of said characters, and how little energy we get daily. 2. Lack of content - this is definitely a side game but since everything but PvP can be finished instantly with skips, you can do everything for the day in <5 minutes. I love this game and want to play it more. Please add more modes so there is more to do on a daily basis! 3. Banner rates feel really, really bad - rate up characters hardly have any drop priority, and with the spark at 200, you can easily dump your entire pyroxene stash on a single character. 4. PvP is straight up terrible - it's all on auto and can't be controlled so the AI makes their typical dumb decisions and costs you the win more often than not. It's actually painful to watch, to the point where some people start a match and reboot the game so they don't have to. On top of that, the PvP rewards aren't worth it, so the mode is almost skippable entirely. 5. Censorship - devs promised they wouldn't do this and that it's not their fault, but that's hard to believe. It's a slippery slope and sucks to see happen to my favorite game. I really really wanted to like this app but it just feels like such a step backwards from Viewranger (VR). Have been testing it in the high mountains (Snowdonia) in mixed weather and have found myself reverting back to VR whenever I have a time of need. Things which are much better in VR: - The UI when navigating - in cold or wet weather, particularly with gloves, you don't want to be trying to pinch the screen to zoom in an out. The compass with the + and - on either side on VR is far easier to use for zooming in and out on the go. - The long thin red arrow showing direction of movement is much clearer and easier to interpret in VR than the very small blue arrow in OA. - The lack of detailed contour lines without zooming ridiculously far in is so so frustrating. VR landscape maps and OS maps show these even when zoomed out to a decent distance. I find them an essential navigational feature in the mountains. - OA seems to stop navigation/recording when minimized for long periods. I often have VR/OA operating in the background whilst hiking and just get it out when needed. With OA it seems to lose everything when re-opened whilst VR records without fail. - One of the key navigational features it misses is that on VR the cross hair shows your current altitude and location, if you move the crosshair over other bits of your route it not only shows you the altitude at that point, but also distance from yourself to that point as the crow flies...this is so helpful for judging distances en-route. - I'm sure there's more things but that's all I can think of from the top of my head. Currently, I wouldn't rely on OA for hiking in the mountains whilst I've heavily relied on VR for years in the mountains. In fact, I'd pay triple my previous subscription to keep VR. Really hoping OA improves over time as it's definitely the inferior product at present for mountain hiking. I'll keep testing it intermittently.

Its functional but a gutted version of the previous app, Google play music. Download any other streaming app instead. Here are the issues with it in no particular order. Core features that should be functional are not. The auto play is never truly disabled, instead when an album ends YTM seems to randomly decide from the top 100 what to play next, often doesn't even match same genre I was listening to. The shuffle button is broken and almost always starts on the same song and runs through a preset "shuffled" version of the playlist often repeating the same subset of songs (about 10 songs) over and over. Songs cannot be reordered in the app, users must use youtube on desktop to change the order of songs in their playlist. This is an issue for both music streamed from the servers as well as music that is downloaded onto the device. Desktop users are not supported except through user created apps, which would mean giving account log in information to an unauthorized third party. Users on desktop cannot download previously purchased MP3 files so even if a user wanted to transfer their collection to a different service it's too late and YTM is holding digital collections hostage. Files can only be downloaded on mobile devices but are not the original quality purchased or the original quality uploaded. Instead all the files downloaded are highly compressed mp3 files. Overall this is a massive leap backward from google play music and in my opinion not even a real competitor to other music streaming or music playing apps. The only advantage to using YTM vs other apps is the apps ability to download any youtube video in the 'music' category as an mp3 onto a mobile device, but I am sure that this is a bug and will be patched out soon as it is legitimately a form of pirating music (downloading songs that haven't been paid for).

My family and I were making vacation plans and I was the main person booking the vacation home. To book it, I had to have the down payment from a single account so the 3 other families joining me sent their portion of the vacation home down payment to me via Zelle. All was looking good, I received all 3 payments and sent vacation home down payment. After a couple of weeks, 1 family wanted to send their remaining portion. They informed me Zelle would not let them send it to me. I went to my Zelle app and thought, maybe I should reinstall. I did and it said my number was invalid. I called customer service and they said I had been flagged for suspicious activity and misuse and there was nothing I could do and nothing they could or would do. I'm certain some notification could have been sent prior to this whole fiasco to alert me of the possibility of misuse and discontinuance. I am very disappointed in Zelle to say the least! If I could I would give it a "0 stars". A family member works at a bank and sees plenty of people using Zelle to move large amounts of money (some more than 10x the amount I received) with no issues. Why pick on the little guy trying to book a vacation for his family. Customer service on this particular incident, in my opinion, was nothing more than a person reading a script to move me through the system to get to the next person. The "supervisor" they connected me with was just as bad, not helpful at all. So now my family must choose a different form of online banking transfer to complete our vacation home booking. What a waste and disappointment. I understand Zelle needs to take precautions on banking transfers but seriously, a little investigation before revoking usage could help reduce "0" star reviews.
